affiliation: Department of Data and Decision Sciences, Emory University
paragraphs: At Emory University, I study Applied Mathematics and Statistics under the mentorship of Prof. Ruoxuan Xiong.

My work lies at the intersection of machine learning and statistics, with a focus on understanding how models behave in imperfect, real-world settings. I am particularly interested in situations where data is incomplete, biased, or evolving, and how these challenges affect the reliability of learning systems.

More broadly, I think about machine learning not just as a predictive tool, but as a system that must remain trustworthy under uncertainty. My work often draws on ideas from statistics and causal inference to better understand and improve model behavior.

I have worked on a range of applied problems—including multimodal healthcare modeling, applied NLP, and sequential decision-making—which has allowed me to study these questions across different domains.
